1.2.2.5-f17.accuracy_reason: The passage runs from Georgics 1.417 to 422, not 417–420, because 'concipiunt' is in line 422. Burton also drops line 421 ('nunc alios, alios dum nubila ventus agebat'), not just line 419. So the note's line range and its account of what he left out are incomplete.

1.2.2.5-f18.accuracy_reason: Horace, Satires 1.1.36 reads 'inversum contristat Aquarius annum'.

1.2.2.5-f32.accuracy_reason: Mundus alter et idem (c. 1605) is a satirical imaginary voyage published under the name Mercurius Britannicus and generally attributed to Joseph Hall.
